hub_grid.title: Hub Settings
hub_grid.description: Your grid connection and the site-wide policy applied to whatever inverters and batteries you add. Inverters, batteries and their PV arrays are configured separately — add an Inverter / Home Battery once the hub exists.

data.phase_a_current_entity_id: Sensor that measures grid current for phase A (optional - set to 'None' for off-grid setups)
data.phase_b_current_entity_id: Sensor for phase B current (optional - set to 'None' for single-phase)
data.phase_c_current_entity_id: Sensor for phase C current (optional - set to 'None' for single/two-phase)
data.enable_max_import_power: Create max import power limit slider
data.max_import_power_entity_id: Sensor for maximum import power (optional override)

data_description.main_breaker_rating: The amperage rating printed on your main circuit breaker. Used to calculate maximum safe power draw per phase.
data_description.invert_phases: Enable if your CT clamp reads negative values when importing power from the grid. Common with some Shelly and Eastron meters.
data_description.enable_max_import_power: When enabled, creates a slider to limit total import power (default = breaker x phases x voltage). Uncheck to disable the limit entirely.
data_description.max_import_power_entity_id: Advanced — use a template sensor or input_number instead of the built-in slider. When set, takes precedence over the slider.
data_description.phase_voltage: Typically 230V in Europe, 120V in North America.
data_description.grid_export_limit: The site's physical or contract ceiling on grid export. Excess mode triggers once export comes within the trigger margin of this limit, and with a battery capacity and solar forecast on the battery page it enables the PV clipping forecast. 0 = no export limit: Excess never triggers on export and the forecast is off.
data_description.excess_trigger_margin: How far below the export limit Excess mode engages. Inverters curtail slightly under the limit, so a trigger exactly at the limit would never fire.
data_description.site_update_frequency: How often grid sensor values are read. Does not affect how often charging commands are sent to chargers.
data_description.auto_detect_phase_mapping: Monitors charger current draws to detect incorrect phase wiring. Works for all charger types on multi-phase sites. Disable if false alerts occur.
data_description.solar_grace_period: In Solar and Excess modes, how long to keep charging at minimum current when conditions are no longer met before pausing. Set to 0 to pause immediately.
data_description.battery_soc_hysteresis: Prevents rapid on/off switching near SOC thresholds. E.g., with 3% hysteresis and a 90% target, charging resumes at 87% and pauses at 90%.
data_description.base_consumption: Typical daytime MINIMUM house draw. Forecast production above export limit + this value counts as unplaceable — entering a peak figure disables the feature in practice.
data_description.forecast_soc_floor: The recommended max battery SOC never drops below this, however large the forecast surplus.

data_description.inverter_max_power: Nameplate rated power from your inverter's datasheet. Set to 0 to skip inverter limits entirely.
data_description.inverter_max_power_per_phase: Usually total power divided by the number of phases. Set to 0 to skip per-phase inverter limits.
data_description.inverter_supports_asymmetric: Most hybrid inverters (Deye, Victron, Huawei) support asymmetric output. SolarEdge and Fronius are typically symmetric.
data_description.wiring_topology: Parallel: inverter and grid feed independently (AC-coupled solar, no battery). Series: all power flows through the inverter (hybrid inverter with DC-coupled battery).

inverter_config.title: Inverter
inverter_config.description: Add an inverter as a power source on this hub. A site can have several (e.g. an older AC-coupled string inverter plus a new hybrid) — the hub aggregates the whole fleet.

data.name: Name for this inverter
data.inverter_output_phase_a_entity_id: Inverter output sensor for phase A (optional)
data.inverter_output_phase_b_entity_id: Inverter output sensor for phase B (optional)
data.inverter_output_phase_c_entity_id: Inverter output sensor for phase C (optional)

data_description.inverter_max_power: Nameplate rated power from this inverter's datasheet. Set to 0 to leave unconstrained.
data_description.inverter_max_power_per_phase: Usually total power divided by the number of phases. Set to 0 to skip per-phase limits.
data_description.inverter_supports_asymmetric: Most hybrid inverters (Deye, Victron, Huawei) support asymmetric output. SolarEdge and Fronius are typically symmetric.
data_description.wiring_topology: Parallel: this inverter feeds the grid bus directly (AC-coupled solar, no battery). Series: power flows through this inverter (hybrid with DC-coupled battery).
data_description.solar_production_entity_id: Optional — if left empty, solar production is calculated from grid export + household consumption. Only set this if your inverter provides a direct solar power reading.
data_description.solar_forecast_device_ids: Forecast devices from the Open-Meteo Solar Forecast integration — it creates one device per PV array, so select each array's device. With the grid export limit and battery capacity set, enables advisory sensors recommending how full the battery may get before the midday production peak.

inverter_battery.title: Inverter Battery
inverter_battery.description: The battery physically behind this inverter — leave everything empty if it has none.

data_description.battery_power_entity_id: Must read a POSITIVE number while the battery is discharging (supplying power) and negative while charging. If your sensor is inverted, wrap it in a template sensor to flip the sign.
data_description.battery_soc_full: SOC at or above which THIS battery counts as full and stops absorbing excess solar.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: The kWh this battery's SOC percentage spans (usable capacity). Used for the fleet SOC weighting and the PV clipping forecast.

inverter_control.title: Battery Charge Control
inverter_control.description: Optional. Lets the PV clipping forecast slow this battery's charging on days when the midday peak would otherwise be clipped at the export limit — the battery stays lower in the morning so there is somewhere to put the surplus. Leave empty to skip; nothing is ever written to your inverter until you also turn on the Battery Charge Control switch.

data.inverter_charge_limit_entity_id: Battery charge limit entity to control (optional)

data_description.inverter_charge_limit_entity_id: The inverter's own maximum battery charge current/power number entity (Deye: 'Battery Max Charge Current'). Leave empty to keep this inverter advisory — the forecast still publishes its recommendation as a sensor, nothing is written. Setting it adds a Battery Charge Control switch, which must be turned on before anything is written.
data_description.inverter_charge_limit_unit: Deye and most hybrids take DC amps at battery voltage; some inverters take watts. The recommendation is computed in watts and converted.
data_description.battery_voltage_entity_id: Used for the watts-to-amps conversion. More accurate than the nominal value across the charge curve; the nominal is used when it is missing.
data_description.battery_nominal_voltage: Fallback for the conversion — 51.2 V for a 16S LFP pack, 25.6 V for 8S.
data_description.inverter_charge_limit_normal: Written back when the forecast releases the limit, in the same unit as the target entity. 0 restores the entity's own maximum, which is where an unmanaged inverter sits.
data_description.inverter_charge_control_interval: These registers go over Modbus and some firmwares write them to EEPROM, so writes are paced rather than sent every cycle.
data_description.inverter_charge_control_deadband: As a percentage of the normal charge limit. A new recommendation closer than this to what the register already holds is not written.

data.name: Name for this device
data.plug_switch_entity_id: Switch entity that controls the plug on/off

data_description.entity_id: Used as a prefix for sensors created by this integration (e.g., sensor.<prefix>_power).
data_description.plug_power_rating: The power this device draws when turned on. Used for allocation calculations. Ignored when a power monitor sensor is configured.
data_description.plug_max_current: The plug's hardware current rating — its socket/relay limit. Caps the current the engine will route to this plug; separate from the set power above.
data_description.connected_to_phase: Which electrical phase(s) this plug is wired to. Determines which phase capacity is used in calculations.
data_description.charger_priority: Lower number = higher priority. Only affects distribution in Priority and Sequential modes.
data_description.plug_power_monitor_entity_id: When set, the actual measured power is used instead of the fixed power rating for more accurate allocation.
data_description.update_frequency: How often to re-evaluate whether this plug should be turned on or off.
data_description.solar_grace_period: In Solar and Excess modes, how long to keep the load on at minimum when conditions are no longer met before turning off. Set to 0 to turn off immediately.

power_station_config.title: Portable Power Station Configuration
power_station_config.description: Configure a portable power station (EcoFlow Delta and similar) as a modulating load. Load Juggler sets its charge rate from available power, and uses its backup reserve as the on/off gate.

data_description.entity_id: Used as a prefix for entities created by this integration.
data_description.station_charge_speed_entity_id: The station's AC charging speed control. Load Juggler writes the charge rate it allocates here.
data_description.station_reserve_entity_id: The station's backup reserve level. This is the on/off gate: below the current battery level the station stops drawing from the wall and runs its own loads from its battery.
data_description.station_battery_level_entity_id: State of charge. Used to free the station's allocated power for other loads once it is full.
data_description.station_charge_limit_entity_id: The station's own maximum charge limit. The reserve is never raised above it, so your battery-health cap is respected. Defaults to 90% if not set.
data_description.station_ac_input_entity_id: Total power drawn from the wall. With the AC output sensor it isolates the charging component — anything plugged into the station is household consumption, not this load's draw.
data_description.station_ac_output_entity_id: Power the station is supplying to its own outputs. Subtracted from AC input to get the charge rate.
data_description.station_min_charge_power: The lowest rate the station accepts (200 W on EcoFlow Delta models). Below this it cannot charge at all, so the reserve is dropped instead.
data_description.station_max_charge_power: The most the station may draw. Set below the hardware's own maximum to cap it.
data_description.station_normal_reserve: Held day to day. The station discharges down to this level to run its own loads, and charges no further from the grid.
data_description.station_storm_reserve: Held while the Storm Reserve switch is on — charged from any source and not discharged below.
data_description.solar_grace_period: How long to keep charging at minimum when solar/excess conditions are no longer met.

hot_water_tank_config.title: Hot Water Tank Configuration
hot_water_tank_config.description: Configure a hot water tank controlled through a climate entity (for example a Generic Thermostat).

data.name: Name for this device
data.tank_prioritize_below_normal: Prioritize over other solar-priority loads when below normal temperature

data_description.entity_id: Used as a prefix for entities created by this integration.
data_description.climate_entity_id: The climate entity regulating the tank. Load Juggler reads its temperature and controls its on/off state and target setpoint.
data_description.heating_element_power: Rated power of the heating element — used for power allocation when no power sensor is configured.
data_description.tank_away_temperature: Minimal / frost-protection setpoint. Used by Freeze Protection mode and as the low end of Solar Priority.
data_description.tank_boost_temperature: High target used when surplus energy is available or the battery is above its target SOC.
data_description.connected_to_phase: Which electrical phase(s) the heating element is wired to.
data_description.charger_priority: Lower number = higher priority. Only affects distribution in Priority and Sequential modes.
data_description.tank_power_entity_id: Optional sensor reporting the element's live power draw — used instead of the fixed rating when present.
data_description.tank_power_device_id: Optionally pick the smart relay/outlet powering the tank; its power sensor is resolved automatically.
data_description.update_frequency: How often to re-evaluate the tank.
data_description.solar_grace_period: In Solar Priority mode, how long to keep heating at minimum when conditions are no longer met before stopping.

data_description.evse_maximum_charge_current: The highest current your charger supports. Check your charger's manual.
data_description.charger_l1_phase: Only change if your charger is wired differently and/or you see unexpected behaviour regarding per-phase power limits.
data_description.charger_l2_phase: Only change if your charger is wired differently and/or you see unexpected behaviour regarding per-phase power limits.
data_description.charger_l3_phase: Only change if your charger is wired differently and/or you see unexpected behaviour regarding per-phase power limits.

charger_timing.title: Units & Timing
charger_timing.description: Configure charge rate unit and timing settings

data_description.charge_rate_unit: Most OCPP chargers use Amperes. Some chargers (e.g., certain Wallbox models) require Watts instead.
data_description.profile_validity_mode: Absolute uses timestamps, Relative uses durations. Try Absolute first — switch to Relative if your charger doesn't respond correctly.
data_description.update_frequency: How often to send updated charging profiles to this charger.
data_description.ocpp_profile_timeout: How long a charging profile remains valid. The charger reverts to default behavior if no new profile is sent within this time.
data_description.charge_pause_duration: When allocated current drops below the minimum, the charger is held at 0A for this duration before recalculating. Prevents rapid start/stop cycling.
data_description.stack_level: OCPP protocol parameter. Only change if your charger ignores charging profiles at the default level.
data_description.solar_grace_period: In Solar and Excess modes, how long to keep charging at minimum current when conditions are no longer met before pausing. Set to 0 to pause immediately.

priority.title: Device Priority Order
priority.description: Pick the devices in the order you want them served — the first one you select is priority 1 (served first when power is contended), the next is priority 2, and so on. To change the order, remove the chips and re-add them in the order you want. Any device you leave out keeps its current ranking at the end. Note: an operating mode's urgency tier can still override this order.

data_description.charger_l1_phase: Only change if your charger is wired differently and/or you see unexpected behaviour regarding per-phase power limits.
data_description.charger_l2_phase: Only change if your charger is wired differently and/or you see unexpected behaviour regarding per-phase power limits.
data_description.charger_l3_phase: Only change if your charger is wired differently and/or you see unexpected behaviour regarding per-phase power limits.

charger_timing.title: Update Units & Timing
charger_timing.description: Update charge rate unit and timing settings

data_description.charge_rate_unit: Most OCPP chargers use Amperes. Some chargers (e.g., certain Wallbox models) require Watts instead.
data_description.profile_validity_mode: Absolute uses timestamps, Relative uses durations. Try Absolute first — switch to Relative if your charger doesn't respond correctly.
data_description.update_frequency: How often to send updated charging profiles to this charger.
data_description.ocpp_profile_timeout: How long a charging profile remains valid. The charger reverts to default behavior if no new profile is sent within this time.
data_description.charge_pause_duration: When allocated current drops below the minimum, the charger is held at 0A for this duration before recalculating. Prevents rapid start/stop cycling.
data_description.stack_level: OCPP protocol parameter. Only change if your charger ignores charging profiles at the default level.
data_description.solar_grace_period: In Solar and Excess modes, how long to keep charging at minimum current when conditions are no longer met before pausing. Set to 0 to pause immediately.

data_description.circuit_group_current_limit: The amperage rating of the circuit breaker shared by the loads in this group.
